body.statement: For the separate case \(S=\varnothing\), the selected mean table is empty, \(\mathcal I_{\varnothing}(\pi;\varnothing)=[0,1]\) for every \(\pi\in\mathcal F\), and \(\overline W(\varnothing)=1\). This is a deterministic population-width statement with no assignment or randomization distribution.
body.justification: Separating the empty panel prevents a degenerate zero-arm object from being treated as a randomized experiment.
body.gap: The empty-panel boundary is a design-domain clarification rather than a novelty claim; it records the population width implied by the sharp-width identity.
body.consumer: Implementations can return the deterministic no-trial benchmark without constructing an invalid allocation or assignment law.
